sections.name: capture_context
sections.content: Owner reflection, 2026-08-23, at the close of the Pattern Grid arc (srs#435: audit → charter → preference layer → layer rules → compass → enforcement stack). The tension-based decision process behind the charter is a method the owner has developed for years; this application — the grid, the axis preferences with boundary clauses, the cell preferences, the enforcement substrate — is its most practical instantiation so far. This note captures WHY the form works and why its famous predecessors failed in application, as background meaning for the charter. It builds on the earlier capture 'Fundamental Tensions as the Generative Root' (fundamental-tensions): that note argues tensions come first and generate principles; this one is about the transmission problem — what happens to tension statements after they are written down.

sections.name: the_internalized_map
sections.content: When a spec or a piece of software is designed well by one skilled human, a version of this tension map is internalised as taste: the felt sense of which pole should win in this situation and what would justify the exception. This is Polanyi's tacit knowledge — we know more than we can tell. Tacit taste works, but it does not transfer, cannot be audited, does not scale past one skull, and dies with the practitioner. The field's historic dichotomy: tacit judgment (true but trapped) versus codified rules (transferable but inverting on contact with institutions, because rules specify behaviour, and behaviour can be complied with meaninglessly).

sections.name: how_the_agile_manifesto_inverted
sections.content:
The Agile Manifesto is a masterwork of tension-statement craft — the charter's cell preferences borrow its 'X over Y' form directly. Its failure in application was mechanical, not moral, and each mechanism is specific:

1. NO BOUNDARY CLAUSES. It states each preference plus one global qualifier, but never says when the right-hand pole legitimately wins. Without that, the statement degrades in two directions at once: absolutists read 'over' as 'instead of'; institutionalizers invert it outright.
2. THE LEGIBILITY GRADIENT. The right-hand poles (processes, tools, documentation, contracts, plans) are billable, certifiable, auditable; the left-hand poles are tacit. Institutions metabolize what is legible, so without a mechanism actively defending the left poles, economic gravity alone inverts the statement. Large-scale 'agile' frameworks are not a betrayal of the manifesto so much as what a boundary-clause-less tension becomes when it meets an organization.
3. NO SUBSTRATE. No decision records, so every consultant became a de facto interpreter and interpretation drifted toward commercial incentive; no supersession mechanism, so it froze in 2001; no review trigger, so 'this clause keeps being overridden' could never formally register as the map being wrong.

Christopher Alexander's pattern languages met the same fate by the same mechanisms: generative process metabolized into template catalogs — form captured, weighing lost.

sections.name: what_the_charter_form_does_differently
sections.content:
The tension form as instantiated in the SRS charter codifies the WEIGHING rather than the behaviour — which is the part of taste that was supposed to be uncapturable. A boundary clause is taste written down: not 'do X' but 'X wins unless these named conditions hold, and here is what the exception must prove.' Checked against the manifesto's failure mechanisms: every preference carries its boundary clause (both the absolutist and the invertor must argue with explicit text); every preference is located in a cell and on an axis, so it cannot be quoted out of context because context is structural; the map evolves by ruled supersession (rename-is-a-migration, successor decisions) instead of freezing or forking into an interpretation market; the review trigger — a clause overridden twice for the same reason is a finding against the clause — gives the map a formal way to be wrong.

And the piece the manifesto's era did not have: an always-present practitioner. The internalized map historically beat the written one because the skilled human consults theirs at every decision at zero cost, while the written one sits in a drawer. Agents change that arithmetic — the externalized map can be applied as continuously as the internalized one ever was, and auditable where taste never was. The method's practicality was never really about the lenses; it was about whether the surrounding system could afford to keep consulting them.

sections.name: the_reflexive_risk
sections.content: This stack can still invert, and the inversion would look like charter COMPLIANCE: alignment sections written as boilerplate, cell tokens applied ritually, the compass becoming this project's own process-over-judgment framework. The defenses are deliberate: the enforcement guards check presence, never quality (guards cannot judge judgment); 'a proposal that lands in no cell is a finding against the grid, not against the proposal' is the escape valve; and the mechanism's suspicion is pointed at itself — the thing protected by every tension statement is on its left-hand side and cannot be proceduralized. The manifesto's authors were right about that; they were wrong that the defense was to build nothing. The defense is the minimum mechanism that keeps the weighing present.

sections.name: why_this_lives_in_srs
sections.content: The mission statement ranks the sharing of practice — fields, types, blueprints, protocols — above the sharing of content itself. An internalized design sensibility made portable (tensions, boundary clauses, precedents, and their evolution, as typed records that travel) is exactly that sentence made real. The Agile Manifesto could not carry its own meaning forward; the charter is being built inside a system whose entire purpose is that meaning carries. Portability cell (♓): the charter as travelling practice is the mission's own proof case.

sections.name: graduation_trigger
sections.content: Rung 0 by the repo's capture ladder: this is background meaning — not a ratified decision (no alternatives-with-costs) and not structure (the grid's cells, axes and preferences will be Tier-2 data when the charter self-hosts). GRADUATION: when srs#273's charter self-hosting lands the matrix as typed records, this note graduates via derived-from into the rationale that accompanies them (a design note or the matrix records' evidence base). Until then it stays here, linked from the Decision Compass (#461) as background reading.

sections.name: research_verdict_2026_08_23
sections.content:
The precedents research (decision-layering-precedents, 2026-08-23) tested this note's thesis adversarially across constitutional law, standards bodies, safety-critical operations, TRIZ, organizational systems, and ethics frameworks. VERDICT: the thesis survives in a narrower, stronger form.

NARROWED: boundary clauses are NOT the necessary cure. Durable systems survive on bare preferences (the HTML Priority of Constituencies, RFC 1958, Ross's duties, Ostrom's principles) when they have some OTHER cheap, legitimate way to record contextual exception, disagreement, uncertainty, or learning at the point of application: precedent and distinguishing, waivers with compensating controls, graded recommendation strength, dissent, local rule-making, or an explicit rule that empirical feedback outranks doctrine. The stronger formulation: PRINCIPLE SYSTEMS INVERT WHEN THE INSTITUTION HAS NO CHEAP, LEGITIMATE WAY TO RECORD EXCEPTION, DISAGREEMENT, UNCERTAINTY, OR LEARNING AT THE POINT OF APPLICATION. Boundary clauses are one such mechanism among several, and where a strong case tradition exists, a case record plus exception machinery can beat them.

CONFIRMED STRONGLY: the presence claim (systems stay influential only when embedded in the control surface of work — courts, waiver processes, line-stop, review tooling) and the substrate claim (every apparent bare-principle survivor turns out to have substrate — social, procedural, or legal, not necessarily technical; the requirement is that application leaves institutional memory that can affect the future rule).

NEW PATHOLOGY NAMED, beyond this note's reflexive-risk section — AUTOMATED RITUALIZATION (Bridgewater the type specimen, Cynefin's 'zombie enforcement' the general form): premature classification (forcing open cases into known cells because a citation must be produced), metric substitution, interpretive centralization (whoever controls prompts and ontology becomes the constitutional court), chilling effects (only machine-legible objections travel), and self-sealing doctrine (contrary evidence explained as non-compliance). The charter's defenses must include a formal path for findings AGAINST the charter, and the useful distinction that principles come in kinds — reasons, defaults, tests, rules — of which only the latter two need explicit exception machinery at the clause level.

The research's adoption shortlist (distinguishing, waivers, dissent records, force/confidence grading, decision-mode classification, the empirical override, amendment jurisdiction, graduated guard vocabulary) is dispositioned on srs#435.

title: Taste Made Portable: why tension statements invert, and what defends them
